history.name: Handing a task to a coding agent
history.description: The commands that prepare work for a coding agent — bootstrap, audit, review, redraft check and style rewrite — print a prompt for you to paste. Add --copy to put it on the clipboard, or --run claude, codex or gemini to hand it to that agent and wait; any other command that reads a prompt on stdin works too. When the agent stops, you see its last message, whether it recorded what its task asks for, and the command that resumes its session. Nothing is handed to an agent unless you pass --run.
history.dev_notes: One file per agent in src/agents/ (claude.mjs, codex.mjs, gemini.mjs, custom.mjs), each with the headless command line, a parser for its event stream and its resume command; index.mjs is the registry and resolves --run (a bare --run reads $LEDGER_AGENT or config.json "agent"), runner.mjs spawns it in the project root with the prompt on stdin. src/prompt.mjs holds TASKS: how to call each brief and the stamp to check afterwards; an agent that exits without it returns exit code 3. Claude runs with acceptEdits and an allowlist of ledger and read-only git commands; Codex with --sandbox workspace-write. The Claude and Codex adapters were tested against the real CLIs; the Gemini one follows its documented headless mode and has not been run against a live install.
